name: Yasuní National Park
story: Yasuní National Park is a protected rainforest in Amazonian Ecuador covering roughly 10,000 km2 between the Napo and Curaray Rivers. Designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1989, it is an exceptionally biodiverse habitat harboring numerous species of trees, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
matters: The park lies within the Napo moist forests ecoregion and holds approximately one-third of the total native bird and amphibian species of the Amazon. It serves as an important ecological convergence point for the Equator, Andes Mountains, and the Amazon rainforest.
